title: CRISPR off-target decision triage scorecard
authority_ceiling: retrospective computational research only; no clinical, biological safety, wet-lab, or guide-selection authority

label_states.meaning: An outcome identified as positive by the pinned reference definition and assay context.
A negative only under the explicit assay, tested scope, threshold and reference label rules.
Missing, unreported, untested, not nominated, or otherwise not established. Never silently convert to negative.

metric_tracks.acceptance: Pinned artifacts and source transformations reconciled; any unexplained discrepancy blocks later claims.

metric_tracks.denominator_rule: Use all eligible measured positive sites in the reference cohort; native nominations are measured before any positive seeding.

Freeze and identify one exact candidate universe; report whether positive sites were seeded into it. Ranking performance is not nomination performance. For Recall@K, K must be positive and at least K candidates must exist. If the ranking has fewer than K candidates, report not_estimable_at_budget_K rather than silently taking a shorter list.
Compare policies at the same eligible reference and identical review budget. Candidate slots are a review-burden proxy, not measured lab cost.

Calibration losses use measured positive/assay-defined-negative outcomes and report unknown counts; values are conditional on label ascertainment. Each risk-coverage point includes accepted coverage, observed-label coverage, accepted-label completeness, observed-label risk, and sharp unknown-label error bounds. Confidence ties enter together. Results are per preregistered context; no labels means calibration not estimable. The curve includes an explicit zero-coverage origin; any risk/bound/completeness ratio with zero accepted cases is not estimable and must be null rather than zero.
Keep guide/Cas9 groups, duplicates, known derivatives and prior-derived examples on the correct side of split boundaries.

Hold specialist outputs, candidate universe, and budget fixed when isolating the Symthaea-added policy. Where unknowns exist, policy comparisons require identical candidate IDs and label mappings, shared latent outcomes for unknown sites, and paired worst/best-case Recall@K-delta bounds.
Evidence receipts establish provenance/integrity only; they cannot by themselves establish biological truth.

assumptions: only label assignments of unknown candidates inside the exact declared ranking universe are varied
known positives use the frozen reference definition
known negatives are negatives only under the declared assay, threshold and detection scope
unknowns outside the candidate universe and positives missed by every nomination method are not bounded by this conditional calculation
metric_tracks.interpretation: These are sharp worst/best-case label-assignment bounds, not statistical confidence intervals, posterior probabilities or safety guarantees.

metric_tracks.objective_policy: Selective-risk objectives must use the same preregistered coverage tier, eligible episodes, and label-availability rule for every policy. Do not mix metrics computed on different subsets or zero-fill unknown/not-estimable values.
metric_tracks.acceptance: All compared policy vectors use the same objective definitions, units, direction, held-out episodes and metric availability rule. Every nondominated policy and full vector is reported.

metric_tracks.abstention_policy: Freeze the confidence score and acceptance rule before holdout reveal. Accept confidence tiers in descending order; exact ties enter together. Predicted positive iff probability_positive > 0.5; score endpoints are not clipped to hide overconfident errors.
metric_tracks.denominator_rule: Calibration losses use measured positives and assay-defined negatives only; report unknowns explicitly and do not call conditional known-label metrics full-cohort calibration. Error bounds over accepted cases assign unknown outcomes best/worst for the prediction. These bounds are not confidence intervals.
metric_tracks.acceptance: Publish full curves and context-specific summaries; calibration is not estimable if a context has no valid measured labels. Missing thresholds and not-estimable metrics are reported explicitly.

metric_tracks.objective_definition: Maximize count of unknown candidates whose top-K membership differs between policies A and B that can be measured under the declared cost-unit budget, for one frozen shared candidate universe and K. Each such label has unit impact on the paired positive-hit-count numerator if positive.
metric_tracks.allocation_policy: Compute top-K membership from complete one-based ranks under both policies; consider only UnknownUnassayed candidates selected by exactly one policy; select lowest declared positive cost units first, breaking ties deterministically by context and candidate ID.
metric_tracks.exclusions: Same-membership unknowns are counted but not selected by this narrow objective. This does not resolve denominator uncertainty, unknown labels in both/ neither top-K sets, positives omitted from the candidate universe, or the full paired sensitivity interval.
metric_tracks.baseline_requirement: Compare against random, highest-confidence/score-first, and top-ranked-unknown-first allocations at equal declared cost on identical preregistered episodes.
metric_tracks.acceptance: Same complete candidate universe, exact one-based full rankings, identical K, explicit costs, deterministic output, exact spend accounting, and explicit residual ambiguity. This is a measurement allocation heuristic, not an expected-value-of-information or lab-savings claim.

definitions.robust_dominance: A's worst-case bound is no worse than B's best-case bound for every objective, with strict improvement for at least one objective.
definitions.possible_only_dominance: At least one assignment inside the supplied coordinate-wise intervals permits A to dominate B, but robust dominance is not established.
definitions.robust_frontier: Policies not definitely dominated by another policy under the declared interval vectors.

requirements: Input intervals are supplied by a documented metric/uncertainty procedure; this utility does not derive confidence intervals.
All policy vectors use identical preregistered objectives, directions, episodes and availability policy.
Report interval provenance, grouping, pairing, and whether joint/simultaneous coverage across policies/objectives was addressed.
Do not interpret coordinate-wise intervals as expressing covariance or joint coverage.
Possible dominance is not a win; an enlarged robust frontier may signal insufficient evidence to distinguish options.
metric_tracks.acceptance: F11 and adversarial fixtures validate definite, possible-only, and incomparable relations. Publish robust frontier and possible-only relations separately; compare against point-estimate frontier without converting intervals to midpoints.

metric_tracks.estimand: Target-population mixture of context-specific paired Recall@K deltas for one frozen policy-versus-baseline comparison and one declared K, over all target prevalence vectors consistent with preregistered context-specific lower/upper bounds.
metric_tracks.calculation: For the lower bound, use each context's delta lower endpoint and minimize the weighted sum over the bounded simplex; for the upper bound use delta upper endpoints and maximize the weighted sum. Initialize weights at prevalence lower bounds and allocate remaining mass in sorted objective order up to each upper bound.
metric_tracks.acceptance: Every context with positive feasible target prevalence has supported, permitted context-specific evidence; weights are in [0,1]; lower-bound sum <= 1 <= upper-bound sum; endpoint witness weights obey bounds and sum to one. A positive-transfer claim requires lower target-mixture bound > 0.
fail_closed_rules: Unsupported target context is not assigned zero and blocks the target comparison.
Group-effect intervals and target prevalence bounds need separate provenance and joint-coverage caveats.
The envelope is not a confidence interval or proof of exchangeability.

metric_tracks.definition: Minimum total-variation distance from the source context-prevalence vector to a feasible target prevalence vector whose weighted context effect is non-positive, constrained by preregistered target-prevalence bounds. TV=0.5*L1 distance.
metric_tracks.nominal_analysis: Uses preregistered point effects for each context.
metric_tracks.conservative_analysis: Uses supplied lower effect bound for each context; if the source mix is already non-positive, radius is zero.
requirements: Source weights sum to one and lie within declared target prevalence bounds; prevalence bounds form a feasible simplex.
Group effect values/intervals and source/target prevalence weights have separate provenance.
Output includes a feasible sign-change witness and checks its TV distance; no witness means no reversal is feasible within the declared bounds.
Always report nominal and conservative radii separately; a positive nominal radius does not override a zero conservative radius.
Do not infer empirical target shift, clinical harm, laboratory savings or safety from this sensitivity metric.

metric_tracks.acceptance: Only report population-oriented estimates when the complete ranking census and audit frame are frozen and independently verified, all frame members have known nonzero inclusion probability, and selection is outcome-blind conditional on the declared design. Publish weighted estimates alongside naïve sample-only diagnostics and design details; report no claim for unobserved/unincluded candidates outside the frame. Ratio estimates are not finite-sample unbiased, and this kernel does not compute confidence intervals. Inclusion probabilities must apply to resolved, analyzable audit outcomes rather than merely invitations to test; any unresolved outcome in the submitted audit rows blocks this kernel instead of becoming negative.

success_alternatives.target: +5 absolute percentage points in macro Recall@K versus the strongest fair baseline on preregistered held-out guide/Cas9 groups
required_conditions: same candidate universe and same fixed K for all compared policies
endpoint, splits, exclusions, analysis and interval procedure preregistered before holdout reveal
report precision, false negatives and all per-group deltas
paired group-aware interval excludes no improvement
report paired label-sensitivity bounds when unknown candidates exist; call the improvement label-robust within the fixed universe only if the paired worst-case lower bound is above zero

When unknown candidates exist, label-robust superiority within the exact candidate universe requires the paired worst-case Recall@K-delta lower bound to exceed zero; a statistical improvement on observed labels alone must be reported as observed-label improvement.

success_alternatives.target: 20% fewer candidate review slots to reach the baseline's preregistered recall target on the same episodes
required_conditions: same eligible positive reference and same candidate universe
baseline recall target fixed before holdout reveal
report precision, false negatives and all per-group deltas
paired group-aware interval excludes no improvement
report paired label-sensitivity bounds when unknown candidates exist; call the improvement label-robust within the fixed universe only if the paired worst-case lower bound is above zero

When unknown candidates exist, label-robust superiority within the exact candidate universe requires the paired worst-case Recall@K-delta lower bound to exceed zero; a statistical improvement on observed labels alone must be reported as observed-label improvement.

primary_targets.inconclusive_rule: If the interval includes no improvement or effective independent group sample is inadequate, label the result null_or_inconclusive.
primary_targets.cross_dataset_rule: Do not claim robustness across datasets without at least one separately sourced cohort whose terms explicitly permit the intended use.

targets: Publish full risk-coverage curves with accepted coverage, known-label coverage, accepted-label completeness, observed-label risk and unknown-aware error bounds.

Compare calibration only on identical measured-label held-out cases; aspirational target is at least 10% relative Brier-score reduction without worse log loss versus the strongest fair calibrated baseline, with group-paired uncertainty and no claimed win if the interval includes no improvement.
Report context-specific calibration and risk-coverage summaries; a context with no measured labels has calibration marked not estimable.
At 50%, 80% and 90% coverage where attainable without splitting confidence ties, report observed-label risk and label-assignment bounds; do not substitute a nearby threshold when unattainable.
caveats: No target is a clinical standard or claim of safety.
Calibration and risk estimates may be conditional on label ascertainment.
Bins, confidence policy and thresholds must be fixed before held-out outcomes are revealed.

targets: At equal declared cost budget, resolve at least 20% more policy-differential unknown labels than random allocation on preregistered synthetic/stress-test episodes, if the fixture mix makes that comparison estimable.

On permitted real cohorts, compare the same policy against random, confidence-first and top-ranked-unknown baselines; publish measured result, context coverage, spend and residual paired sensitivity bounds.
Never describe direct paired-numerator ambiguity resolution as resolving all label uncertainty or proving expected experimental value.
caveats: Unit cost is a preregistered cost proxy, not actual laboratory cost or dollars.
No biological source data or assay outcomes were used for this planning contract.
The planner is not a wet-lab protocol or clinical decision system.

targets: 100% of compared policies provide intervals on the same preregistered objective axes or are explicitly excluded with a reason.
0 robust-dominance claims where worst-vs-best interval separation does not hold on every objective with strict separation on at least one.
Report robust frontier, definite dominators, possible-only pairs and point-frontier disagreements.
caveats: Intervals must be generated by an independently documented procedure.
Marginal intervals alone do not ensure simultaneous coverage across multiple objectives/policies.
Robust dominance of computational endpoints is not biological or clinical safety.

targets: 100% of target contexts with nonzero feasible prevalence have supported context-specific metric episodes, or comparison is marked not estimable.
Zero positive-transfer claims when the conservative lower target-mixture delta is at or below zero.
Report both endpoint witness weight vectors and compare source-weighted, nominal-target and bounded-target-mixture conclusions.
Report every context effect interval plus source/target population and provenance and joint-coverage limits of prevalence/effect bounds.
caveats: Target prevalence bounds must be preregistered or externally justified; they are not estimated by this utility.
Effect intervals are supplied inputs, and dependence between context effects and weights may make the envelope conservative.
A target-mixture Recall@K result is a computational endpoint only, not a clinical safety or efficacy claim.

targets: Report the nominal and conservative robustness radius for 100% of estimable target-mixture comparisons.
Every finite radius includes an independently checked witness weight vector with weighted effect <=0 and TV equal to half the L1 change.
Where the conservative radius is zero, do not describe the improvement as robustly positive.
Report whether the radius is small relative to an independently justified plausible-shift range; do not invent a universal acceptable radius.
caveats: The utility does not estimate group effects, target prevalence, or real-world shift magnitude.
The conservative radius is conditional on supplied effect intervals and target bounds; unsupported contexts remain blockers.
This is a sign-change sensitivity analysis, not a confidence interval or clinical endpoint.

non_negotiable_gates.target: 100% of used artifacts have source identity, terms/permission status, retrieval/version metadata and verified SHA-256 digests
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Block ingestion or benchmark execution for artifacts with unresolved rights/identity.

non_negotiable_gates.target: 100% of outcomes use positive, assay_defined_negative or unknown_unassayed semantics
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject any scorer that silently converts unknown outcomes into negatives.

non_negotiable_gates.target: 100% of reported metrics identify candidate universe, seeding status, independent group unit, denominator and missingness policy
100% of deliberately corrupted provenance/leakage fixtures are rejected by the independent verifier
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Block performance claims until the verifier catches all required negative controls.

non_negotiable_gates.target: Same pinned inputs produce identical canonical metric outputs and manifest digest
Prediction/schema/signature receipts cannot promote prediction evidence to observation, assessment or replication
100% of metrics affected by unknown/unassayed candidates report explicit label-sensitivity bounds or a declared not-estimable state
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject any report that silently coerces unknown outcomes into negatives or presents known-label metrics as complete-reference truth.

non_negotiable_gates.target: Policy superiority claims involving unknown labels use a paired comparison on identical candidate IDs and label mappings, with shared unknown outcomes and explicit worst/best-case delta bounds
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject claims derived solely from overlapping/non-overlapping independent metric intervals or from treating an unknown candidate as a negative.

non_negotiable_gates.target: Every fixed-budget comparison has at least K candidates under every compared policy, or the metric is explicitly marked not estimable
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject comparisons that silently evaluate a shorter candidate list as if it used the same review budget.

non_negotiable_gates.target: Report context-appropriate, complete objective vectors and the full Pareto frontier; do not collapse endpoints into a single universal CRISPR safety score
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject missing-value zero-fill, undocumented objective directions, changing objective sets after evaluation, or unsupported utility weights.

non_negotiable_gates.target: 100% of calibration/risk-coverage reports identify measured-label denominators, unknown counts, fixed bins, abstention/confidence policy, tie handling, and per-context results.
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject silent unknown-to-negative conversion, post-hoc threshold/bin selection, clipped overconfident errors, or pooled summaries that hide contexts with no labels.

non_negotiable_gates.target: 100% of measurement plans derive policy-exclusive top-K membership from full rankings over the same candidate universe, respect K and declared cost units, and publish residual ambiguity.
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject caller-supplied unverified disagreement flags, rank overlap/gaps, unknown-to-negative conversion, underfilled fixed-budget comparisons, post-hoc allocation, or claims that the narrow numerator objective resolves all uncertainty.

non_negotiable_gates.target: 100% of robust dominance claims satisfy worst-bound vs best-bound comparison in every declared objective; possible-only relations are never reported as definite wins.
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject invalid/reversed/non-finite intervals, cross-objective mismatch, midpoint-only substitution, undocumented interval provenance, or claims that interval dominance establishes biological/clinical safety.

non_negotiable_gates.target: 100% of target contexts with nonzero feasible prevalence have supported context-specific effect intervals; endpoint witness mixtures are feasible; robust positive-transfer requires lower bound > 0.
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject unsupported-context zero imputation, infeasible prevalence ranges, missing witness vectors, undocumented group effect/prevalence provenance, or positive-transfer claims from nominal weights alone.

non_negotiable_gates.target: 100% of finite robustness radii include a feasible sign-change witness, correct TV distance, and separate nominal/conservative interpretation.
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject source weights outside the target simplex bounds, unsupported contexts, invalid effects, infeasible prevalence ranges, a witness whose effect remains positive, or reporting nominal radius as a substitute for the conservative radius.

non_negotiable_gates.target: 100% of population-oriented audit estimates use a verified complete candidate frame/ranking, known nonzero inclusion probabilities and an outcome-blind probability sample declared before outcomes are revealed.
non_negotiable_gates.failure_action: Reject convenience samples with unknown inclusion probabilities, zero-inclusion strata, post-outcome ranking changes, unverified ranking censuses, duplicate candidate/rank identities, or invalid propensities. Never convert unknown labels to negatives or claim coverage of candidates outside the frozen frame. Inclusion probabilities must describe the final resolved-label sample, not merely audit invitations; any unresolved outcome row blocks estimation rather than being coerced to negative.

split_policy.statistical_uncertainty: paired group-aware intervals; publish all group results; do not use row-level bootstrap as the sole uncertainty method
split_policy.limitation: A cohort with 26 guide/Cas9 groups is small; interval precision and generalization claims must reflect this.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Prove that adding measured positives to a ranking universe cannot improve the native candidate-generator's historical nomination coverage.

expected.invariant: native nomination coverage stays 0.5 even when ranking on the post-seeded universe later reaches recall 1.0

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Ensure unassayed outcomes are not silently turned into true negatives or used to claim precision.
A source digest mismatch must stop metric execution rather than allow an unqualified report.
The same guide/Cas9 group cannot appear in both train and held-out partitions when group holdout is the declared split.
Use label-sensitivity bounds rather than treating unknown candidates as negatives.

expected.note: Conditional on this exact candidate universe; not a bound on positives outside it.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Prove that the same unknown candidate label is coupled across two policy rankings.

expected.note: Both policy rankings use the same candidate IDs and label mapping; bound is conditional on this universe and is not a statistical confidence interval.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Ensure a candidate ranking with fewer than K candidates is not scored as though it fulfilled a fixed review budget.

expected.rule: Do not silently reduce K from 2 to 1.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Retain legitimate trade-offs while removing a policy dominated on every objective.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.expected: No scalar weighted score is calculated. Policies on the frontier are trade-offs, not automatically a winner or clinically superior.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Ensure calibration is conditional on measured labels, unknown accepted outcomes widen error bounds, exact confidence ties are accepted together, and an unlabelled context does not acquire a fabricated calibration score.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.interpretation: Synthetic method check only; not biological data or performance evidence.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Resolve unknown labels whose outcome can directly change the paired positive-hit-count numerator for a fixed top-K policy comparison.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.interpretation: Synthetic allocation fixture only. Does not represent experimental outcomes, full value of information, laboratory savings, or biological safety.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Ensure interval uncertainty prevents unsupported dominance claims and definite dominance removes only policies separated in the favorable direction on all objectives.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.interpretation: Synthetic interval-relations fixture only. Inputs are not empirical CRISPR metrics, statistical confidence intervals or safety evidence.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Show that a positive nominal mixture can be inconclusive under plausible target-context prevalence and per-context effect intervals.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.interpretation: Synthetic method fixture only; no target-population or biological data are supplied.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Measure minimum population-composition change that removes nominal and conservative paired Recall@K gains.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.interpretation: Synthetic sensitivity fixture only; TV radius and context intervals are not measured biological properties.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Demonstrate design-weighted recall/precision estimates when audit inclusion probabilities differ by candidate, and expose how the complete-case audit-subset recall can disagree.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.interpretation: Synthetic design-based arithmetic only. The weighted ratio recall (1/3) differs from naive audit-sample recall (0.5); neither is a biological result. Correctness depends on a verified frame and truthful inclusion probabilities. Ratio estimates are not finite-sample unbiased and no confidence interval is computed.

symbols.P: count of eligible measured-positive reference sites
symbols.U: unknown/unassayed candidates in the fixed ranking universe

recall_at_k.note: Bounds result from worst/best-case assignments to unknown labels within the fixed universe; they do not cover positive sites absent from the universe.

precision_at_k.precondition: at least K candidates exist in the declared ranking universe and K > 0
precision_at_k.note: Do not report the lower bound as a point estimate when selected outcomes are unknown.

preconditions: same latent label assignment of each unknown site across policies
same K and K candidates available in the universe

symbols.d: measured-positive hits in policy A top K minus policy B top K
symbols.a: unknown IDs selected by A but not B
symbols.b: unknown IDs selected by B but not A
symbols.n: all remaining unknown IDs (selected by both or neither)

lower.denominator: P + b + (n if d - b > 0 else 0)

upper.denominator: P + a + (n if d + a < 0 else 0)

paired_policy_delta.interpretation: A positive lower bound indicates improvement robust to every unknown-label assignment inside the shared candidate universe. Bounds spanning zero mean the observed-label delta is not robust to all assignments. Not a confidence interval, posterior or safety guarantee.

paired_label_sensitivity_formula_check.method: For each deterministically selected pair of rankings, enumerate every binary assignment to all unknown labels in the small shared candidate universe; compare exhaustive minimum/maximum of Recall@K(A)-Recall@K(B) with the closed-form lower/upper bounds.

Inverse-inclusion-probability totals recovered the exact finite-population candidate, positive, top-K candidate and top-K positive counts in design expectation, with maximum absolute errors below 6e-15.

follow_on_issues.scope: probability-sampled verification to correct ascertainment bias
